newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Chaos bloodies Taiwan's constitutional assembly.
newsitem.headline: Chaos bloodies Taiwan's constitutional assembly.

text.p: Taiwan's constitutional reform process degenerated into chaos on Wednesday as National Assembly deputies punched, kicked and gouged each other to the point where blood flowed. Two deputies were hospitalised.

In scenes that looked more like Saturday's Tyson-Holyfield heavyweight boxing melee than a political forum, state television showed deputies from rival parties engaged in furious battle around the speaker's dais.
Some deputies jumped on to the speaker's table, while others attacked colleagues with flying kicks, bare fists and choke holds.
One deputy from the fledgling New Party was beaten seriously during the minutes-long chaos, with blood streaming from the back of his head. Another New Party deputy was taken unconscious to hospital.

The National Assembly, an increasingly marginalised elective body whose sole function is to revise the constitution, has been reviewing a package of amendments proposed by the ruling Nationalist Party, which dominates its membership.
Negotiations over the proposals were continuing.
